On one hand, forgetting can be a natural part of the healing process, allowing individuals to let go of painful memories or traumatic experiences that no longer serve a constructive purpose. It can also create a false sense of security, making people less likely to seek alternative information or consider potential consequences. On the other hand, when there are too many genuine choices, it may lead to indecision or regret, as people struggle to evaluate and commit to a single option.

This can lead to regret, dissatisfaction, and a diminished sense of control. As corporations amass immense influence, they may prioritize profit over public interest, resulting in income inequality, labor exploitation, and a lack of regulation.
